newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares surge in speculative trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares surge in speculative trade.

text.p: Speculation about Nigeria's forthcoming 1997 fiscal budget drove share prices higher on Tuesday, dealers said.
The all-share index closed at 6997.84, up from 6988.28 on Monday.
"There is no new information to move the market except speculation about the budget," one dealer said.
Nigeria's cabinet met in the capital Abuja on Tuesday to consider the budget which is widely expected to introduce measures to stimulate economic growth in the country.
Prices were generally higher in Tuesday's trading.
West African Portland Cement Company rose 35 kobo to 47.05 naira but Ashaka Cement and Benue Cement fell 10 kobo and five kobo, respectively at 16.30 naira and 7.10 naira.
The price of textile group Afprint was unchanged despite fire in one of its warehouses on Monday, traders said.

Conglomerate UAC finished eight kobo stronger at 7.50 naira on improved investor perception while traders angling to reap from Nigerian Bottling Company's recent merger caused its shares to end 10 kobo higher at 29.30 naira.
Oil shares surged on undiminished demand. Total added 20 kobo to 58.40 naira, Unipetrol gained 29 kobo at 59.62 naira and Texaco closed at 34.60, up 20 kobo.
Surplus shares of Guaranty Trust Bank forced its price to dip 20 kobo to 11.00 naira while container firm Van Leer fell 10 kobo to 12.20 naira due to declining profitability.
